title: What If the Moon Kept Drifting Away From Earth?

scenes.text: What if the Moon kept drifting away? It is, at the speed your fingernails grow.
Lasers bounced off the Moon show it moving away by about three point eight centimeters a year.
Its tides act as a brake on Earth, making each day less than two milliseconds longer every century.
Run the tape back. About three hundred and fifty million years ago, a year had around three hundred and eighty-five days.
One point four billion years ago, a day lasted only about eighteen hours.
And just after the Moon formed, simulations suggest Earth spun once every six hours.

description:
What if the Moon kept drifting away?
It already is: about 3.8 cm a year. Tides slow Earth's spin, so days were shorter in the past, perhaps 18 hours 1.4 billion years ago.
What should we run through next?
